NASA just highlighted how their first space 3D printer made a socket wrench aboard the space station. But what if future astronauts 3D-printed an entire moon base directly out of lunar soil? Instead of hauling heavy steel into orbit, autonomous rovers could melt lunar dust—called regolith—layer by layer using lasers or concentrated sunlight. Scientists are already testing regolith mixtures to build airtight shelters, landing pads, and radiation shields right on the lunar surface. Would you volunteer to live inside a printed moon house? Follow for more what-ifs.
